drafts.label: Reply · competence vs tutor (personal noticing)
drafts.body:
yeah the "drain out of my fingers" part is the honest half most people skip.

tutor mode and competence theft ride the same tool. the difference is whether you named the skills you're trying to keep in your hands.

pick the few that matter. sweat those. agent the rest without pretending it's the same kind of knowing.
drafts.why: Grounded in OP: AI robs competence; drain from fingers; amazing tutor; pick competence areas and do work there; pair with agent otherwise. Take: name skills to keep vs same-tool different knowing. Stay in craft/builder world — no school stamp.

drafts.body:
yeah handing finished CSS instead of design adjectives is the whole trick.

"make it pretty" is fog. a stylesheet the model can't rewrite mid-output is a real standard.

skills beat vibes when quality has to survive the next chat.

drafts.label: Short · don't rush the smart reply
drafts.body:
A friend sent me a long voice note after a hard week.

I almost replied with a tight little paragraph of advice.

Deleted it. Sent back: "I'm here. Tell me the part that still hurts."

He talked for another four minutes.

Sometimes the rare skill isn't knowing what to say.
It's not rushing to be the smartest person in the thread.
drafts.why: Independent values/listening pillar — not mashup of competence boundaries or CSS skills.

quality.notes: Independent insight: restraint in reply can be rarer than smart advice. Story hook/scene: voice note + deleted advice + 'part that still hurts'. Finish/like/comment: last line; seeds recognition replies. Not pack collage.
